condition: suspected acute spontaneous pneumothorax presenting with sudden severe resting dyspnea while seated in a collegiate rower
level_rationale: Sudden severe shortness of breath while sitting still today in a 20-year-old collegiate rower indicates an acute cardiopulmonary emergency such as spontaneous pneumothorax or pulmonary embolism requiring immediate emergency department pulse oximetry, chest radiography, and stabilization, whereas mild shortness of breath occurring during hard rowing sprints over the past month points to suspected exercise-induced bronchoconstriction warranting non-emergent outpatient physician evaluation and spirometry.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 20, collegiate rowing team participation, and sudden severe shortness of breath while sitting still today) with an equal-length 15-word vs 15-word span swap and 8 shared trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). Under Rule A first choice and Rule D, changing only the severity and provocation of shortness of breath in f3 from acute severe resting dyspnea today to recurrent mild dyspnea during hard rowing sprints this month coheres tightly with collegiate crew while shifting care from ER (level 4) to outpatient clinic evaluation (level 2) with zero stated negatives.
